Generate one synthetic sample from a peak catalog

Source: R/catalog_generation.R
generate_one_synthetic_from_catalog.Rd

For each compound in the catalog, a Bernoulli(prevalence) draw decides whether the compound "fires" in this sample. If it fires, a 2-D Gaussian peak is placed at compound$rt_loc, compound$cv_loc with morphology bootstrapped from the compound's observed (sigma_rt, sigma_cv, intensity) triples. Per-peak location and size jitter apply on top. Folded-Normal noise is added at the end when add_noise = TRUE.

Usage

generate_one_synthetic_from_catalog(
  catalog,
  H,
  W,
  add_noise = TRUE,
  size_jitter = 0.15,
  location_jitter_rt = 2,
  location_jitter_cv = 1,
  noise_scale = 1,
  prevalence_override = NULL,
  intensity_mult = NULL,
  compound_ids = NULL,
  peak_shape = c("gaussian", "emg", "mix"),
  emg_tau_range = c(0.2, 0.8),
  emg_mix_prob = 0.3
)

Arguments

catalog

A peak_catalog object from build_peak_catalog().

H, W

Output image dimensions in pixels.

add_noise

Whether to add folded-Normal background noise.

size_jitter

Per-peak log-Normal size scale factor SD.

location_jitter_rt, location_jitter_cv

Per-peak location jitter SD (pixels).

noise_scale

Multiplier on catalog$noise$sd. Default 1.0.

prevalence_override

Optional named numeric vector mapping compound_id (as character) to a replacement prevalence. Not present compounds use the catalog's own prevalence.

intensity_mult

Optional named numeric vector mapping compound_id (as character) to an amplitude multiplier applied when the compound fires. Defaults to 1.0 for unlisted compounds.

compound_ids

Optional integer vector of compound_ids to include; NULL (default) uses every catalog compound.

Value

List with clean (H x W), noisy (H x W, = clean when add_noise = FALSE), and fired (logical vector of length nrow(catalog$compounds) indicating which compounds actually appeared in this sample).

Details

Compared to generate_one_synthetic(), the catalog version reflects the real-data property that the same compound positions appear across many samples. Which specific compounds appear per sample is random (via Bernoulli), but the compound identities and positions are shared across all synthetic samples.
